name: nist-sp800-53_to_asd-ism
description: Crosswalk from NIST SP 800-53 control ids to ASD ISM control ids (ism-NNNN). The ASD ISM OSCAL release carries no per-control NIST cross-reference, so this table is a PROPOSED mapping derived by matching NIST control intent against ISM control statements. It MUST be reviewed and signed off by a compliance authority before being relied on. Each source id maps to one or more target ids; keys match case-insensitively; unmapped ids pass through unchanged (see oscal/crosswalk.py). Note: a source id mapped to multiple targets asserts the component satisfies ALL of them, so all targets must be in the active baseline for declared <= baseline to hold. Mappings are intentionally 1:1 to the single closest ISM control; alternates are listed in `provenance` for review, not applied.

ac-3.ism_statement: Privileged users are assigned a dedicated privileged user account to be used solely for duties requiring privileged access.
alternates: ism-1507 (privileged access requests validated when first requested)
ac-3.rationale: Access enforcement via privileged/standard account separation; in scope for Essential Eight 'restrict administrative privileges'.

ia-5.ism_statement: Multi-factor authentication uses either: something users have and something users know, or something users have that is unlocked by something users know or are.
alternates: ism-1402 (credentials protected by password manager/HSM, full ISM only)
ia-5.rationale: Authenticator management is represented in Essential Eight by the multi-factor authentication controls. For service/database credentials specifically, ism-1402/ism-1685 are closer but sit outside ML1.

sc-8.ism_statement: An ASD-Approved Cryptographic Protocol (AACP) or high assurance cryptographic protocol is used to protect data in transit.
sc-8.baseline: FULL ISM only (NOT in any Essential Eight ML profile)
alternates: ism-1277 (data between database and web servers is encrypted)
ism-1139 (only the latest version of TLS is used)
sc-8.rationale: Transmission confidentiality maps to the AACP-in-transit control. The Essential Eight does not cover transmission cryptography, so this target is absent from the E8 ML baselines; verifying it requires the full ISM catalog (or a classification system profile) as the active baseline.

sc-13.ism_statement: An ASD-Approved Cryptographic Algorithm (AACA) or high assurance cryptographic algorithm is used when cryptography is used.
sc-13.baseline: FULL ISM only (NOT in any Essential Eight ML profile)
alternates: ism-0471 (only AACAs used by cryptographic equipment, applications and libraries)
sc-13.rationale: Cryptographic protection maps to the AACA control. As with sc-8, this is outside Essential Eight scope and needs the full ISM catalog as the active baseline to verify.
